items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: I waited up there with Buddy playing that Jitney dance a long time, just playing the horn.

ctx.x: He's still real good I think. He still plays good I think. Yeah, George plays nice. I mean Edmund Hall. I haven't heard him for three years. You got one of his records, didn't you? Yeah. I was going to ask, did you always use four strings on your bass or sometimes three? Always did use four strings. Have you ever used a three?

Well I'll tell you, I bought a bass with the same bass I tell you about with the old man. Well he had three strings on that bass. Bill and Moran. Yeah, Bill and Moran. Well after that third, that fourth string, I go to make a G, like sometimes I'm playing a soft number and I have my bow and I will make a low G, you know what I mean? Well I couldn't make my low G. Sometimes I have to finger my G down from this F, you see? And if I didn't finger that G I'd have to make that open G. What I mean by making a G open…
Yeah. That was pretty. Yeah, that was good. I was going to ask you about this band. If you had any pieces that you all composed, or did Buddy ever write any music? Do you know of any songs?
